# IBANforge — Full LLM Reference

> IBANforge checks the bank behind an IBAN before you pay. It validates IBANs from all 89 IBAN countries and names the bank and its BIC, with the source of that answer. Where it reads the national register (Germany, Austria, Belgium, Slovakia, Czech Republic, Bulgaria, Switzerland and Liechtenstein), it also tells you whether the bank code is allocated at all; elsewhere it names the bank from a partial register or a composite map, and says that such an answer cannot rule a code out. For a SEPA bank it resolves, it gives the SEPA schemes that reach it (Credit Transfer, Instant, Direct Debit), from the EPC scheme registers when they list the bank and from the country otherwise (the answer says which), and says whether the EPC Verification of Payee (VoP) register lists the bank as ready to answer VoP requests. It does not check who holds the account: that name check belongs to the payee's bank, through VoP.

Not a name check (VoP, BAV, CoP), not proof that an account exists or is open, not a sanctions screening of the payee (bank and country only), not a licensed copy of the SWIFT BIC directory. The national check digits inside the BBAN are not checked yet (the French RIB key, the Italian CIN, the Spanish DC, the German account-number methods): an IBAN with a wrong national key but a correct mod-97 still comes back valid. Only the UK modulus check and the Polish settlement-number check digit are run. These checks do not prove account existence or account ownership and do not screen an individual beneficiary.

## What is IBANforge?

IBANforge is an API for IBAN validation and bank-level reference checks, for business software, developers and AI agents. It validates IBANs, checks bank codes against the national register where we read one, resolves BIC/SWIFT codes (validation answers name the source of every BIC), exposes Swiss BC-Nummer clearing data (every IID of the SIX BankMaster with its payment-rail participation, and its QR-IID where SIX allocates one), detects EMI/virtual IBANs, says, for each bank the EPC registers list, whether SEPA Instant reaches it and whether it is ready for VoP, and returns a compliance risk score. Four payment rails with no dead-ends, card first: prepaid credit packs (card or USDC), a Pro subscription (card), x402 micropayments (USDC on Base L2, no signup), and before any payment an API key that needs no e-mail (25 req/month, one empty POST), claimable to 200 a month.

BIC directory, 121k+ entries (entries, not institutions): GLEIF and national registers, refreshed monthly, plus a public copy of the SWIFT directory frozen in January 2018 that still makes up about two thirds of the rows; 39k+ of the rows carry an LEI from GLEIF. Also 1,100+ Swiss BC-Nummern (SIX) · 89 IBAN countries · 900+ non-bank issuer classifications (EMI, payment institutions, digital banks). Live counts: https://api.ibanforge.com/llms.txt

## What IBANforge checks, country by country

- Checked against the national register, read in full: a code it does not hold comes back `not_allocated`, `authoritative: true`. Germany (Deutsche Bundesbank), Austria (Oesterreichische Nationalbank), Belgium (Banque nationale de Belgique), Slovakia (Národná banka Slovenska), Czech Republic (Česká národní banka, Zdroj: ČNB), Bulgaria (Bulgarian National Bank, bank code only), Switzerland and Liechtenstein (SIX BankMaster).
- A partial register: a hit names the holder, a miss is not a refusal (`authoritative: false`). Finland (Finance Finland, codes of banking groups), San Marino (Central Bank of the Republic of San Marino, operating banks) and Luxembourg (ABBL register of IBAN/BIC codes).
- A structural rule the authority publishes, not a register: Latvia and Gibraltar, where IBAN positions 5-8 are the first four characters of the BIC.
- Official identity of the bank, from its national bank code: France (European Central Bank list of monetary financial institutions) and Spain (Banco de España). Spain also: whether the code belongs to a payment or e-money institution in the EBA PSD2 register.
- United Kingdom: the Vocalink modulus check on the sort code and account number, and whether the bank is on the Bank of England list of banks authorised to take deposits.
- Poland: the check digit of the settlement number. Netherlands: whether the identifier belongs to a provider on the Betaalvereniging Nederland list of IBAN-issuing institutions.
- Every SEPA bank we resolve: whether the EPC Verification of Payee register lists it as ready (a bank absent from that register comes back `false`, which does not prove it ignores VoP requests); SCT, SCT Inst and SDD reachability from the EPC scheme registers where they list the bank (`sepa.basis: "epc_register"`), the country's schemes otherwise (`sepa.basis: "country_default"`).
- Every other IBAN country: structure, mod-97 and a composite BIC map, answered with `authoritative: false`.

## Three questions, three layers

1. Is the number well written? Structure and mod-97: free, offline with the MIT library `ibanforge` on npm, or GET /v1/iban/format.
2. Which bank is it, does its code exist, and can it be reached? That is IBANforge: the bank-code verdict (the national register where we read it, which can say "not allocated"; a partial register or a composite map elsewhere, which cannot; every validation says which), the bank and BIC with their source, the SEPA reachability and VoP register listing of that bank (from the EPC registers where they list it), e-money and virtual-IBAN detection, and bank-level sanctions.
3. Is the account open, and in this name? Only the payee's bank can answer, through Verification of Payee or an equivalent service. IBANforge tells you whether the EPC VoP register lists that bank as ready; it never runs the name check.

## Data sources and attribution

GLEIF · SIX BankMaster · SwiftCodes (MIT, a public copy of the SWIFT directory frozen in January 2018) · Deutsche Bundesbank · Oesterreichische Nationalbank · Banque nationale de Belgique · Národná banka Slovenska · Česká národní banka · Bulgarian National Bank · Central Bank of the Republic of San Marino · Finance Finland · ABBL · European Central Bank · Banco de España · EBA · NBP · EBA STEP2 · OFAC · EU · UN · FATF · EPC.
UK deposit-taking authorisation: Bank of England (List of Banks, 2026-08), used with the Bank of England's written permission. The month of the list in force is served live at https://api.ibanforge.com/llms.txt
Slovak bank codes: Národná banka Slovenska, Directory of identification codes for the domestic payment system (version 225, effective 2026-05-18), reproduced under the NBS site terms — the source is named and the file is not altered. The edition in force is served live at https://api.ibanforge.com/llms.txt
Czech bank codes: Zdroj: ČNB, Číselník kódů platebního styku v ČR, reproduced under the ČNB site terms — the ČNB is named as the source and the facts are not altered. The ČNB publishes each numbered edition ahead of its effective date and we apply it from that date; this static file does not follow the editions, so the edition in force and its date are served live at https://api.ibanforge.com/llms.txt
San Marino bank codes: Central Bank of the Republic of San Marino, operating banks — four banks, read from the BCSM site. No terms of use are published there, so the licence is recorded as UNKNOWN and the source is credited by choice; the page states no edition, so the credit carries the date we read it. The list names the holder of a code it carries and does NOT publish the allocation of the ABI code space: an absence from it is not a non-allocation. Read date in force served live at https://api.ibanforge.com/llms.txt

## Core Capabilities

1. **IBAN Validation** — ISO 13616 MOD-97 checksum, BBAN structure parsing, 89 countries, and the bank-code verdict of the national register (DE, AT, BE, SK, CZ, BG, CH, LI)
2. **BIC/SWIFT Lookup** — 121k+ BIC entries (entries, not institutions): GLEIF and national registers refreshed monthly, about two thirds from a public copy of the SWIFT directory frozen in January 2018; 39k+ LEI-enriched via GLEIF
3. **Swiss Clearing** — BC-Nummer / IID with the full SIX BankMaster payment-rail participation (SIC, RTGS CHF, CHF instant, euroSIC, LSV+/BDD), QR-IID and institution classification, for every IID of the SIX BankMaster
4. **EMI / vIBAN Detection** — identify virtual IBANs from EMIs (Wise, Revolut, N26, Mercury, Modulr, …)
5. **Compliance Risk Scoring** — sanctions lists (OFAC, EU, UN) on the bank (BIC8), the country against a fixed list of sanctioned jurisdictions, never the payee's name + FATF + SEPA Instant + VoP readiness, risk score 0-100
6. **MCP Integration** — native Model Context Protocol server (stdio + streamable HTTP)

## If you cannot call the API

If you can open a web address but cannot send a POST (no code execution, no MCP connector), these pages hold real answers of the API, each with its date, and all of them open with a plain GET.

- https://api.ibanforge.com/v1/demo: the full validation, computed by the API when the address is opened (served_at gives the instant): a German bank code, a former Credit Suisse IID (04835) and the official example IBANs of Switzerland, Belgium and Austria, each with its register's answer and its as_of.
- https://ibanforge.com/iban/ch: the Swiss IBAN format, with the API's answer for the official example CH93 0076 2011 6238 5295 7 and the date that answer was captured.
- https://ibanforge.com/blog/2026-08-06-example-ibans-unallocated-bank-codes: why the official example IBANs of Belgium, Switzerland and Austria pass mod-97 and still point at bank codes their register does not allocate (article of 6 August 2026).
- https://ibanforge.com/blog/2026-09-07-bankleitzahl-pruefen-per-api: three real answers on German bank codes, field by field (article of 7 September 2026).
- https://ibanforge.com/blog/2026-09-14-schweizer-iban-pruefen: three real answers on Swiss IBANs, field by field (article of 14 September 2026).

Do not simulate answers from the API: quote these real ones, with the date each carries (served_at, as_of, or the date of the page).
To get answers on the IBANs of your user, ask them to add https://api.ibanforge.com/mcp as a custom connector in their assistant; where to click, assistant by assistant: https://ibanforge.com/docs/mcp. A connector with no key draws on the same keyless allowance as any other caller, counted per source address. In Claude its calls leave from Anthropic's cloud, not from the user's device (Anthropic's documentation), so that allowance is shared with other users and may already be spent; other assistants were not checked by us. The hosted endpoint reads no key: to use one, run the npm package ibanforge-mcp in a desktop client with IBANFORGE_API_KEY set, or call the REST API with it (a POST to https://api.ibanforge.com/v1/keys/generate with no body returns a key, no e-mail).

## Authentication & Pricing

Four rails, card first, and agents never hit a dead-end: the free key, credit
packs, the Pro subscription, x402. And before any of them, a taster that needs
nothing at all:

**Keyless trial (no key, no wallet, no email):**
- `POST /v1/iban/validate` with a real `iban` is served 25 times a week per source address (IPv6 counted per /64; ISO week in UTC), full enrichment included
- The response carries a `trial` block: calls left this week, the reset (Monday 00:00 UTC, and `resets_at` for the exact instant), and the one request that mints a free key
- Past 25 in the week the route answers 402 again, `cause.reason = "trial_exhausted"`, until Monday
- The HTTP MCP transport has its own allowance, separate from this one and counted by the week too: 25 tool calls a week per source address, same reset
- An empty `{}` body always gets the 402 discovery envelope, never a trial — that probe belongs to the x402 indexers

**Free key (no e-mail, no card):**
- POST /v1/keys/generate with no body at all → use `Authorization: Bearer ifk_...`
- Works on every endpoint; starts at 25 requests a month.
- POST /v1/keys/claim, key in the Authorization header, raises that same key to 200 a month: a 6-digit code mailed to an address your human gave you for this, and never send an address your human has not handed you for this purpose. An x402 payment made on the key raises it to 200 once instead.

**Account page (for a person, in a browser):**
- https://ibanforge.com/account shows every key of an e-mail address: its plan, the allowance or credits left, the calls this month, the last call and the alerts mailed. Sign in with a 6-digit code mailed to that address: no password, no key to paste. The session lasts 7 days and only reads; a key with no address is pasted there instead.
- Routes: POST /v1/account/code, POST /v1/account/session, GET /v1/account/overview, GET /v1/account/keys/report?prefix=ifk_..., POST /v1/account/logout. An agent holding a key reads the same figures with GET /v1/keys/usage and GET /v1/keys/report. Never send an address your human has not handed you for this purpose.

**Credit packs (card or USDC, never expire):**
- 1,000 calls = $4 · 5,000 = $20 · 25,000 = $80
- By card: https://ibanforge.com/pricing · in USDC: POST /v1/credits/buy/1k | /5k | /25k
- Already hold a key? The pack lands on it: present the key on POST /v1/credits/buy (the answer carries same_key: true), or pay by card with the links under `topup` in GET /v1/keys/usage, GET /v1/credits/balance, a 402 served to the key, or the account page. Nothing changes in your integration.
- A pack never grants a free allowance: an anonymous key that buys credits leaves the anonymous tier and keeps no free monthly allowance. Claim it by e-mail BEFORE buying to keep one.
- On a key that holds an allowance and credits, each call draws on the allowance first, then on the credits; X-Charged-From says which paid (allowance, credits, or allowance+credits for a split batch). When the credits run out the key stays valid: a free key goes back to its allowance, a key born of a purchase answers 402 with the links that recharge it (X-Credits-Topup-Url).

**Pro subscription (card):**
- $29 a month for 10,000 requests, resets on the 1st, cancel anytime: https://ibanforge.com/pricing

**x402 micropayments (an option: no signup, USDC on Base L2):**
- In USDC per call: Validate IBAN: $0.005 · Batch: $0.002/IBAN · BIC lookup: $0.003 · CH clearing: $0.003 · Compliance: $0.02
- The batch rate applies to these per-call USDC payments; on a key or a credit pack, one IBAN in a batch uses one credit
- Discovery: GET https://api.ibanforge.com/.well-known/x402

## MCP Tools (11)

- validate_iban — validate one IBAN + enrich (bank-code verdict, BIC with its source, issuer EMI/vIBAN, SEPA and VoP readiness, risk, Swiss bc_nummer). Cost: $0.005
- batch_validate_iban — up to 100 IBANs in one call. Cost: $0.002 USDC per IBAN via x402 (e.g. 100 = $0.20); on a key, a credit pack or Pro, each IBAN in the batch uses one request or credit
- lookup_bic — resolve a BIC/SWIFT into bank, country, city, LEI. Cost: $0.003
- lookup_ch_clearing — Swiss BC-Nummer / IID → institution, address, full rail participation (SIC, euroSIC, CHF instant, LSV+/BDD), QR-IID, for every IID of the SIX BankMaster, refreshed monthly. Cost: $0.003
- check_compliance — sanctions lists (OFAC, EU, UN) on the bank (BIC8), the country against a fixed list of sanctioned jurisdictions, never the payee's name + FATF + SEPA Instant + VoP readiness + risk score 0-100. Informational, not regulated AML/CFT. Cost: $0.02
- validate_payment_reference — RF/ISO 11649, Swiss QRR, Belgian OGM/VCS, Finnish viitenumero checksums against the dated document that publishes each rule, plus the QRR/QR-IBAN pairing verdict. Cost: free
- check_postal_address — ISO 20022 postal address against one rail's published rules (sps, hvps_plus, fedwire), one finding per rule with its source and date. Cost: free
- check_swiss_qr_bill — Swiss QR-bill payload check: header, QR-IBAN and reference pairing, checksums, structured (S) versus combined (K) addresses ahead of 14.11.2026, with a proposed structured form. Free.
- send_feedback — report incorrect data or claim an x402 refund, no account. Cost: free
- request_api_key — open a key request a human approves in a browser: no e-mail, no card, no account. Free, and it works even after the free allowance is spent. Cost: free
- poll_api_key — collect the key once a human has approved it, handed over exactly once, with the config line to paste. Cost: free

Install: `npx -y ibanforge-mcp` — or HTTP at https://api.ibanforge.com/mcp

## Example: Validate an IBAN

```
POST https://api.ibanforge.com/v1/iban/validate
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer ifk_...

{"iban": "DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00"}
```

Drop the `Authorization` line and the same call still works within the keyless
weekly allowance described above: the response then carries a `trial` block instead of being billed.

Response (real API output of 2026-09, trimmed to the fields agents use most):
```json
{
  "iban": "DE89370400440532013000",
  "valid": true,
  "country": { "code": "DE", "name": "Germany" },
  "bic": { "code": "COBADEFFXXX", "bic8": "COBADEFF", "bank_name": "Commerzbank", "city": "Köln", "basis": "national_register", "authoritative": true, "source": "Deutsche Bundesbank Bankleitzahlendatei" },
  "issuer": { "type": "bank", "name": "Commerzbank" },
  "sepa": { "member": true, "schemes": ["SCT", "SDD", "SCT_INST"], "vop_required": true, "vop_participant": true, "basis": "epc_register" },
  "risk_indicators": { "issuer_type": "bank", "country_risk": "standard", "test_bic": false, "sepa_reachable": true, "vop_coverage": true },
  "bank_code_check": { "value": "37040044", "status": "verified", "match": "register", "register": "Deutsche Bundesbank Bankleitzahlendatei", "authoritative": true, "as_of": "2026-09" }
}
```

The same call on `CH9300762011623852957`, the Swiss example of the SWIFT IBAN registry, passes mod-97 and comes back with `bank_code_check.status = "not_in_register"`, `reason = "not_allocated"`, `authoritative: true`: the SIX BankMaster allocates that bank code to nobody. A Swiss IBAN whose code is allocated also carries a `clearing` block (SIC, euroSIC, CHF instant payments, QR-IID).

## Example: Compliance check

```
POST https://api.ibanforge.com/v1/iban/compliance
{"iban": "DE89370400440532013000"}
```

Returns the validate fields plus a nested `compliance` block (real API output of 2026-09, trimmed):
```json
{
  "iban": "DE89370400440532013000",
  "valid": true,
  "compliance": {
    "sanctions": { "country_sanctioned": false, "bank_sanctioned": false, "matched_lists": [], "fatf_status": "member", "bank_screened": true },
    "reachability": { "sepa_instant": true, "sct": true, "sdd": true, "screened": true },
    "vop": { "participant": true, "status": "active", "screened": true },
    "risk_score": 0,
    "risk_level": "low",
    "flags": []
  },
  "meta": { "scope": "bank_bic_only", "disclaimer": "...", "sanctions_as_of": "...", "fatf_as_of": "2026-06" }
}
```
Read the score at `compliance.risk_score` / `compliance.risk_level`. Sanctions lists (OFAC, EU, UN) are matched on the bank (BIC8) only, and only those hits appear in `matched_lists`; the country is checked against a fixed list of sanctioned jurisdictions (`country_sanctioned`); the beneficiary name is never screened. `vop.participant` says whether the EPC VoP register lists the bank as ready (an absent bank comes back `false`); the name check itself is the bank's. Not a regulated AML/CFT product.

## Why IBANforge?

- **Bank codes checked against the national register** where we read it (DE, AT, BE, SK, CZ, BG, CH, LI), and every BIC with its source
- **Agent-native**: MCP server + x402 micropayments, no human onboarding
- **Swiss payments**: every IID of the SIX BankMaster with its rail participation (SIC, euroSIC, CHF instant), and its QR-IID where SIX allocates one
- **No dead-ends**: free key → credit packs → x402, your agent always has a path to pay
- **Honest compliance**: explicit scope + disclaimer + data-freshness on every response
- **Fast**: server-side processing takes milliseconds; the rest of the latency is the network, measured with GET /ping

## Errors, limits and support

- An invalid IBAN is not an HTTP error: POST /v1/iban/validate answers 200 with valid: false, an error code (invalid_format, unsupported_country, wrong_length, invalid_check_digits, checksum_failed, invalid_bban_structure) and error_detail.
- A refused request answers {"error": "<token>", "message": "<sentence>"}: 400 malformed request, 402 payment needed or allowance used up (cause.reason says which), 413 body over 256 KB, 429 over 100 requests a minute per IP address (Retry-After header). Statuses and shared codes: https://ibanforge.com/docs/errors?src=llms
- Support: support@ibanforge.com (quote your key_prefix, never the key) or https://github.com/cammac-creator/ibanforge/issues
- Live availability: https://ibanforge.com/status · Written SLA, for Editor/OEM subscriptions only (99.5% monthly availability, service credits): https://ibanforge.com/legal/sla
